units: <cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 15:2">Targ. Job XV, 2</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Berakhot 18b:14">Ber. 18ᵇ</cite> <he>אחלישתיה לדַעְתֵּיה</he> thou madest him feel badly; <cite ref="Chullin 94b">Ḥull. 94ᵇ</cite>.—
<cite ref="Berakhot 33b:30">Ber. 33ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>לא כיון דעתיה</he> he had not his mind directed on it, recited without devotion.
<cite ref="Berakhot 36a">Ib. 36ᵃ</cite> <he>צנון אַדַּ׳ וכ׳ …</he> people plant radishes with the intention of eating them when they are young.
<cite ref="Berakhot 36a:22">Ib.</cite> <he>מאי דּעְתָּךְ כר״ע</he> (in doing so) what was thy opinion? Is it that thou holdest to R. A.?—
<cite ref="Kiddushin 81b">Kidd. 81ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Berakhot 26a">Ber. 26ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>לאו אַדַּעְתָּאִי</he> I did not think of it.

<cite ref="Ketubot 3a">Keth. 3ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>כל דמקדש אַדַּ׳ וכ׳</he> whosoever betroths a wife to himself does so with the implicit understanding that his act is in agreement with the rabbinical enactments.—
<cite ref="Gittin 70b:10">Gitt. 70ᵇ</cite> <he>ד׳ צילותא</he> a clear mind, full consciousness; <he>ד׳ שגישתא</he> a confused mind, delirium.

<cite ref="Moed Katan 26b:24">M. Kat. 26ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>כמה לית ביה ד׳ וכ׳</he> how little sense (manners) has this scholar!—<he>סלקא דעתך</he> (abbr. <he>ס״ד</he>) it enters thy mind, i.e. you may think.
<cite ref="Berakhot 41b:2">Ber. 41ᵇ</cite> <he>כל שיעוריה ס״ד</he> ‘all its measures’,—you cannot mean that?—

<cite ref="Pesachim 2a">Pes. 2ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>קא ס״ד וכ׳</he> (abbr. <he>קס״ד</he>) thy first impression naturally was that he who said ‘light’ meant really &c. (an editorial remark for the sake of introducing a discussion on premises finally to be upset).
<cite ref="Pesachim 14b:6">Ib. 14ᵇ</cite> <he>דאי ס״ד וכ׳</he> for if we were to think that it was a rabbinical law; <cite ref="Pesachim 18a">ib. 18ᵃ</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Pesachim 18a">Ib.</cite> top <he>ואי ס״ד מכלים וכ׳</he> if we were to assume that he withdrew his opinion only as to vessels &c.; <cite ref="Pesachim 19a">ib. 19ᵃ</cite>; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Sotah 46a:6-8">Sot. 46ᵃ</cite> <he>ס״ד אמינא … צריכא</he> you may possibly think we say, i.e. you may be misled to interpret &c.; therefore (to obviate such a misinterpretation) a Biblical intimation is required; a. fr.
